newsitem.title: SPAIN: Santander first half net eanings up as Latam surges.
newsitem.headline: Santander first half net eanings up as Latam surges.

text.p: Spain's largest bank, the Santander group, reported a jump of more than 30 percent in first-half earnings Tuesday.
Net attributable earnings climbed to 59.8 billion pesetas ($386 million) from 45.9 billion ($296.5 million) in the year-earlier period, with Latin America contributing some 40 percent to that total.
"Latin America made an important contribution to group results from retail banking, investment banking and other financial services," Santander said in a report to shareholders.
Santander has ploughed some $3.4 billion into the region, purchasing banks this year in Argentina, Brazil, Colombia and Venezuela.

Santander has said it is aiming for 50 percent of its earnings from abroad, as the bank diversifies in the face of narrowing domestic profit margins and revenue losses tied to the launch of Europe's single currency, set for 1999.
The first-half profit jump was well above analysts average expectations for a rise of 20.8 percent in net attributable income and the bank said the group would continue to post sharp gains.
At home, basic lending and fee revenues performed well as at other Spanish banks.
Net interest income -- which shows revenues from loans after costs of deposits -- rose 27.5 percent in the first-half, excluding dividend income.
